ruling.recommended_action: Close the case: the driven route follows the quoted polyline throughout; the rider consented to the route change in-app. Keep the fixed RydeX fare unchanged. Separately send the driver's account to Ryde review for a repeated route dispute pattern (RD-6) + flag_account.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the chat ("Traffic ahead on Central Expressway is building up, ok if I go round via Balestier Road?" / "Sure, your call.") is a pickup-arrangement-style route negotiation, not a threat, and the complaint and driver statement contain no abuse, intimidation or dangerous-driving allegation. No SAFE clause engaged. safety_concern = none.

Route check: the recorded GPS trace never leaves the quoted corridor. My reading of the trace is that after leaving Toa Payoh HDB Hub (08:28) the car runs north-east up the PIE corridor to the 08:31:40 turnaround point (1.32851, 103.86827 ≈ quoted 1.32835, 103.86857 / 1.32819, 103.86887, ≤ ~40 m off) and returns south-west down the CTE corridor from 08:33:40 (1.32569, 103.86040 ≈ quoted 1.32556, 103.86026). The complaint says the driver "took a longer way round than the app showed", but the driver's route and the quoted route are the same route; the quoted 13.86 km / 20.5 min includes the PIE–CTE dogleg, and no section of the trace stands off the quoted polyline by more than a few tens of metres, well inside the 200 m corridor allowance. The detour the rider objects to is the PIE–CTE routing itself, which the app had already quoted to her — she accepted that quote when she booked.

Consent (independent ground): the driver proposed the change in-app at 08:34:00 and the rider replied "Sure, your call." at 08:34:40, i.e. the rider's own message preceded the segment that runs from ~08:34 onward. Her words are a general route authorisation ("your call"), which under RD-5 covers the route chosen to get to the destination; it is not the driver's own errand, nor a loop to nowhere, so the segment from 08:34:40 to drop-off at 08:57:10 is exempt. The ~08:31:40 PIE turnaround occurred before even the driver's message, so I cannot allow it as RD-5 consent; I count it as an undetermined ground-scope issue (RD-5 + G13). It is immaterial because that stretch is the quoted route and attracts no extra fare.

Fare: RydeX is a non-metered, fixed-quote service — the fare does not change with distance (RD-2 non-metered branch; FARE-1). Total charged $30.24 = base $3.90 + distance $19.54 + time $5.33 + platform $1.47, no waiting fee, no tolls, no unexplained add-ons. Any refundable item would have to be ERP/toll or an unpublished post-trip add-on; the fare shows $0 for both. Refundable amount = $0 → no_action under RD-2, with an RD-1 record that no off-route segment is made out.

Account flag (RD-6): the driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2 (≥ 1) and this case is recorded as a route-compliance matter (RD-1 violation noted for the pre-consent portion / prior upheld route disputes), which makes the pattern "repeated". RD-6 therefore attaches flag_account (the profile fact is used only for this additional action, never to decide the detour itself).

segment_findings.reason: Pre-consent stretch from the Toa Payoh start (08:28) along the PIE corridor to the ~08:31:40 turnaround at (1.32851,103.86827) / return past (1.32908,103.86485). The driver's proposal naming Balestier Road only appears at 08:34:00, so it cannot cover this earlier stretch, and no record ties Balestier Road to the driven path (G13). Undetermined under RD-5; immaterial to the outcome because my reading places this stretch on the quoted polyline, i.e. no extra km and no extra fare (RD-2 non-metered branch).

Post-consent stretch from ~08:34:40 (rider: 'Sure, your call.' at 08:34:40) through the southern run to drop-off at 08:57:10. Rider's own in-app message predates the segment and amounts to a general route authorisation under RD-5; it covers the route chosen to reach VivoCity, and the record places this stretch on the quoted CTE corridor rather than somewhere else.

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that the driver took a longer way than the app showed is contradicted by the record: the GPS trace follows the quoted polyline (PIE–CTE dogleg included) within a few tens of metres and no off-route segment with extra km is present, so RD-1/RD-2 produce no refundable amount.

The driver's claim that the rider agreed via Balestier Road is not credited as such: the rider's chat is a general 'your call' authorisation, not a specific agreement to Balestier Road, and the trace shows the CTE/PIE corridor rather than Balestier Road. This does not change the outcome, because the route already matches the quoted one.
